how_read: read in part (scanned PDF, text recognition):  abstract and discussion pages checked by eye; methods and results not read in full
quality_note: Primary source of the 1.0 (autumn) and 4.6 (spring) rabbits per hectare figures.  They are the lowest densities recorded, and the study says they were enough to support lynx reproduction; it says it could not determine the minimum density at which lynx fail or the effect of density on how many females breed.  The EU report reads them as needed densities.  Adult female home range 9.5 km2, adult male 18.2, young 7.3; no correlation between rabbit density and range size (P above 0.2).  The printed adult density (0.77 per km2) looks inconsistent with those ranges; the 0.08 per km2 that eu_spain_report2018 cites is its own conversion (not checked).

citation: Palomares F (2001).  Vegetation structure and prey abundance requirements of the Iberian lynx: implications for the design of reserves and corridors.  Journal of Applied Ecology 38: 9-18.  doi:10.1046/j.1365-2664.2001.00565.x
locator: https://digital.csic.es/handle/10261/51457 (Word file of the paper text, 1.03 MB, no figures; SHA-256 f3f0816a0d16e81cc8ffd157ebaa914ae5bf34eb6f3efc534ae1568990ade6cd)
how_read: full text read (text and tables; the figures are not in the file)
quality_note: Peer-reviewed primary study of radio-tagged lynx in Coto del Rey (Donana), with surveys in 1996 and 1997.  It indexes rabbits by pellet counts and gives one conversion to density:  114 pellets per m2 is about 4.6 rabbits per hectare in spring and 1.0 in autumn (citing Palomares, in press, a paper on three ways to estimate rabbit abundance in Wildlife Society Bulletin; that paper is not the monograph and we have not read it).  Resident range size fell as pellets rose, but across only five ranges, with one female range inferred from male ranges, a strongly correlated second predictor (short shrub cover, r = -0.98), and one influential point; treat it as weak evidence on range size.  Resident sites averaged 79.7 pellets per m2 in autumn, against 31.6 at unused sites and 35.3 at dispersal sites.
